lifecycle.implementation_result_summary: D-146-1 and D-146-2 fixed and proven green. D-146-3 is not a product defect in the form the contract assumed: the assertion is unsatisfiable without editing either a forbidden path or the test itself, so it is raised as a finding under AC-146-4 and left for the Operator.

AC-146-1.evidence: proposal_delete_race_never_leaves_workspace_orphans green. Measured cause, not the contract guesses: surrealdb 3.2.0 on RocksDB uses OptimisticTransactionDB with set_snapshot(true) and WRITE-WRITE conflict detection only; get_for_update is never called anywhere in surrealdb-core, so there is no read-set tracking and no SSI. Insert and delete write disjoint keys so neither aborts: the insert ASSERT record::exists reads a snapshot that still holds the workspace, and REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE is a snapshot-bound scan that cannot see a reference key written by a transaction uncommitted at snapshot time. Both contract candidate mechanisms are facets of that one cause. Fix orders the two snapshots via the existing FEMS mutation lock plus an in-transaction existence guard mapped to 404.

AC-146-2.evidence: list_proposals_is_bounded_deterministic_and_workspace_scoped green, including its bounded-limit and workspace-scoping assertions. Cause code-verified: ORDER BY had no status-priority term. Fixed with a SurrealQL-computed status_rank ordered ahead of created_at DESC, proposal_id ASC, so ORDER BY still precedes LIMIT and no Rust-side sort is used.

AC-146-3.evidence: Two compounding causes. (1) list_commit_rows withheld the un-published FR-EVT-MEM-004 until its FR-EVT-MEM-003 sibling was published; fixed by moving that causal rule to dispatch time via commit_event_dispatch_ready. (2) DECISIVE: the test filters pending events on event.payload proposal_id, but validate_memory_pack_built_payload at src/backend/handshake_core/src/flight_recorder/mod.rs:4307 calls require_allowed_keys with a closed 10-key allowlist and an empty optional list, and proposal_id is absent from it; the builder calls validate(), so adding the key would fail every commit. FR-EVT-MEM-004 instead carries its proposal linkage in activity_span_id, as fems-memory-proposal followed by the proposal id. pending_outbox == 2 is therefore unsatisfiable without editing flight_recorder/mod.rs (outside allowed_paths) or the test filter (forbidden by AC-146-4). Raised as a finding; the Orchestrator independently verified it and is routing the decision to the Operator, recommending the filter use activity_span_id while leaving the assertion count and message untouched.

AC-146-4.evidence: No assertion in any of the three tests was weakened, reordered, relaxed or deleted. Every api/memory.rs hunk lies between lines 299 and 1290; the tests module begins at line 1752 and the three tests at 2763 and beyond. The file still contains exactly 29 test attributes, so none was added or removed. The one assertion that could not be satisfied was escalated rather than edited.

lifecycle.blocker: AC-146-3 / AC-146-5: pending_outbox == 2 in commit_outbox_recovers_on_restart_and_preserves_original_evidence_across_later_commits is unsatisfiable within allowed_paths. Requires an Operator decision: either authorise the test filter to use activity_span_id (leaving the assertion count and message untouched), or authorise changing the FR-EVT-MEM-004 payload allowlist in flight_recorder/mod.rs, which is outside this MT allowed_paths.

implementation_findings.summary: FR-EVT-MEM-004 payload cannot carry proposal_id; the test filter is incompatible with the event schema contract.
implementation_findings.detail: flight_recorder/mod.rs:4307 require_allowed_keys enforces a closed allowlist. Recommend the test filter on activity_span_id. Operator decision required per AC-146-4.

implementation_findings.summary: A quarantined FR-EVT-MEM-003 could permanently strand its FR-EVT-MEM-004 sibling, invisible to every listing.
implementation_findings.detail: The old list_commit_rows gate hid a pack-built row until its commit row was published, and unlike the lifecycle outbox there is no requeue path for a quarantined commit-outbox row (only requeue_quarantined_memory_lifecycle_event exists). The gate removal in this MT closes that hole while preserving the ordering guarantee at dispatch time. The change is currently proven only by the suite staying otherwise green; the corrected D-146-3 test would prove it directly. The Orchestrator reviewed this and directed that it be kept rather than reverted.

implementation_findings.summary: Changing an outbox event payload is durable-evidence-affecting.
implementation_findings.detail: ensure_commit_outbox compares row.event_hash against a re-derived event_json_hash, so altering the FR-EVT-MEM-004 payload shape would make pre-existing rows conflict on retry with the message about commit outbox identity being bound to different evidence. Any Operator decision to add proposal_id to that payload must account for existing rows; cold-genesis stores are unaffected.

operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.what_was_asked: AC-146-4 forbids the implementer from editing any assertion in the three target tests and routes 'the test asserts the wrong thing' to the Operator. The implementer established by measurement that commit_outbox_recovers_on_restart_and_preserves_original_evidence_across_later_commits filters pending events on event.payload["proposal_id"], while validate_memory_pack_built_payload (flight_recorder/mod.rs:4307) enforces a closed ten-key allowlist with an empty optional list that does not include proposal_id. FR-EVT-MEM-004 therefore cannot carry that key and the filter can never match it, making the assertion pending_outbox == 2 unsatisfiable by construction.
operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.what_is_authorised: A narrow correction to the SELECTOR ONLY: the test may filter on the field that actually carries the proposal linkage, activity_span_id, in the form fems-memory-proposal:{proposal_id}. The assertion itself is NOT authorised to change - the expected count of 2 and the assertion message stay exactly as written. This is a repair to a filter that cannot match, not a weakening of what the test proves; the assertion's intent, that both the commit and pack-built events survive the crash window un-published and non-quarantined, becomes testable for the first time rather than being quietly impossible.
operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.what_is_not_authorised: Changing the expected count, changing or softening the assertion message, adding proposal_id to the FR-EVT-MEM-004 payload allowlist, or touching flight_recorder/mod.rs. Nothing else in any of the three tests may be edited.
operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.why_the_payload_route_was_rejected: The implementer found (F-146-C) that ensure_commit_outbox compares event_hash, so adding proposal_id to the pack event's payload would change that hash and make pre-existing durable rows conflict on retry. The two routes are not equivalent: correcting the selector touches no durable data, while changing the payload is durable-evidence-affecting on a live store. That finding is what settled the choice.
operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.verification_required: Before choosing the selector, confirm from the source that BOTH FR-EVT-MEM-003 and FR-EVT-MEM-004 carry activity_span_id in the expected form. If the commit event does not, the filter must match both events correctly rather than silently dropping one - a filter that matches only the pack event would make the count wrong in the other direction and would be just as broken as the current one.
operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.effect_on_acceptance: AC-146-3 becomes obtainable and AC-146-5 returns to its original target of 29 passed / 0 failed. If the corrected test still fails, that is a genuine product defect and must be reported as such, not filtered around a second time.

selector_substitution.why: The verification clause in this authorisation required confirming that BOTH FR-EVT-MEM-003 and FR-EVT-MEM-004 carry activity_span_id before the selector was chosen. They do not. build_memory_commit_flight_recorder_event never sets activity_span_id and FlightRecorderEvent::new defaults it to None, so only the pack builder sets it. Filtering on activity_span_id would have matched FR-EVT-MEM-004 alone, dropped FR-EVT-MEM-003, and produced left: 1 again - wrong in the opposite direction. The recommended field was wrong and the mandated check is what caught it.
selector_substitution.substituted_selector_is_correct: trace_id is shared by both events by construction: the commit event is built with stable_uuid("fems-memory-proposal:{proposal_id}") as its trace_id, and the pack event copies commit_event.trace_id. It is scoped to the proposal, and because the listing returns only commit-outbox rows it selects both events of this commit and nothing else. The test derives the same value with its own deterministic_uuid_from_seed.
selector_substitution.independently_verified_by_orchestrator: Checked against the source rather than accepted: zero activity_span_id references in the commit builder at fems_memory.rs:1013-1049; trace_id set from stable_uuid("fems-memory-proposal:{proposal_id}") in that builder; commit_event.trace_id copied at fems_memory.rs:1065; and stable_uuid (fems_memory.rs:1138) and deterministic_uuid_from_seed (api/memory.rs:1659) are byte-identical implementations - SHA256, first 16 bytes, same UUID v4 bit-fixing.
selector_substitution.within_authorisation: Yes. The authorisation text names activity_span_id but its verification clause explicitly contemplates this case: "the filter must match both events correctly rather than silently dropping one". Substituting a field that satisfies that requirement is what the clause directs. Recorded here rather than left silent, because the Operator approved a named field and what shipped is a different one.
selector_substitution.third_route_correctly_refused: The implementer did not add activity_span_id to the commit builder, which would have looked like the obvious fix. That is a product change to a hashed event, and ensure_commit_outbox compares event_hash, so it would have reintroduced the exact durable-evidence hazard (F-146-C) that got the payload route rejected.
selector_substitution.unchanged: Expected count still 2. Assertion message byte-identical. flight_recorder/mod.rs untouched. One line of behaviour changed.

scope.summary: Fix three defects in the memory proposal surface that the restored in-crate test layer exposed: workspace deletion leaves an orphan proposal under a concurrent insert, the proposal list does not put approved proposals first, and the commit outbox restart-recovery path does not reach its expected state. All three are pre-existing behaviour, not regressions from the test restoration.
scope.embedded_mode_boundary: SurrealDB and EventLedger only. No SQLite and no PostgreSQL may be added, restored, imported, or referenced as a live backend.

defects.observed: panicked at src/api/memory.rs:3931: assertion left == right failed: workspace deletion must cascade proposals. left: 1, right: 0.
defects.what_it_means: The test issues delete_workspace and create_memory_proposal concurrently through tokio::join, then counts fems_memory_proposals rows still pointing at the deleted workspace. One row survives. A memory proposal is left referencing a workspace that no longer exists.
defects.code_context: schema.surql line 4886 already declares the workspace_id field on fems_memory_proposals as record<workspaces> with ASSERT record::exists($value) REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE, and delete_workspace_record in storage/surreal/workspaces.rs runs an explicit transaction that clears the Loom dependants and then deletes the workspace, relying on that cascade for the remaining workspace-owned rows. So the cascade is declared, yet an orphan survives under concurrency.
candidate_mechanisms_not_yet_confirmed: The proposal insert evaluates record::exists in a transaction that began before the delete committed, so the assert passes against a snapshot while the cascade has already run, and the insert lands afterwards with nothing left to cascade it.
The SurrealDB reference cascade only reaches rows whose reference was recorded before the delete transaction took its view, so a row created during the delete is invisible to it.
defects.instruction: Confirm which mechanism is real by measurement before changing anything. Do not implement against the guess.

defects.observed: panicked at src/api/memory.rs:2875: assertion left == right failed: approved proposals must lead the actionable projection for crash-safe commit recovery. Observed order was the newer proposal then the approved one; expected the approved one first.
defects.what_it_means: After one proposal is set to approved, the list route must return it ahead of a newer pending proposal, because the actionable projection is what crash-safe commit recovery walks. It does not.
defects.code_context: list_memory_proposals in storage/fems_memory.rs around line 2114 orders strictly by created_at DESC then proposal_id ASC. There is no status priority term, so an approved proposal can never lead a newer pending one. The defect is in the ordering clause, and the diagnosis is code-verified rather than inferred.
defects.instruction: Add a deterministic status-priority ordering term ahead of the recency term, keeping the tie-break stable so the bounded limit case stays deterministic. Do not reorder in Rust after the fact if that would break the LIMIT semantics the test also asserts.

defects.observed: thread 'api::memory::tests::commit_outbox_recovers_on_restart_and_preserves_original_evidence_across_later_commits' (48040) panicked at src\api\memory.rs:4672:9: assertion `left == right` failed: crash leaves the commit (FR-EVT-MEM-003) and pack-built (FR-EVT-MEM-004) events durably un-published and non-quarantined left: 1 right: 2
defects.result_line: test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2112 filtered out; finished in 247.38s
defects.what_it_means: After the simulated crash the test counts the pending commit-outbox events for proposal A and expects exactly 2: the commit event FR-EVT-MEM-003 and the pack-built event FR-EVT-MEM-004, both left durably un-published and non-quarantined. Only 1 is present. One of the two events is either never written on the commit path, or is already published or quarantined at the point the crash is simulated, so the crash window does not preserve the evidence the recovery path is supposed to replay.
defects.code_context: The assertion is at src/api/memory.rs:4672 and filters list_pending_memory_commit_events on the proposal id. The commit path writes into fems_memory_commit_fr_outbox and fems_memory_lifecycle_fr_outbox, both keyed on the proposal with ON DELETE CASCADE in schema.surql. The count is short by one before the recovery poll is ever reached, so the defect is on the write side of the crash window, not in the startup projector.
defects.instruction: Determine by measurement which of FR-EVT-MEM-003 and FR-EVT-MEM-004 is missing from the pending set and why. Do not assume it is the pack-built event. The later assertions about projector recovery and evidence preservation across a second commit are unreached today, so they must also be proven once the count is right.

execution_constraints: CARGO_TARGET_DIR must be an owner-scoped child of ../Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target/ with a SHORT slug. Bundled DuckDB C++ headers hit the MSVC 260-character path limit and fail with C1083 if the target path is long; enabling long paths in the registry does not help cl.exe.
HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT must be set to the absolute artifacts root or embedded_test_backend refuses to start.

Each test opens its own RocksDB store and takes roughly four minutes end to end, including a 30 second shutdown drain. The full 29-test suite took 2175 seconds on this host. Budget for that rather than assuming a hang.

Every run on this Windows host also emits a teardown cleanup failure and leaves the store directory behind. That is separate, is disclosed on MT-123, and must not be mistaken for a defect in this work.
Do not touch api/flight_recorder.rs or workflows.rs: MT-145 owns those.
scope.risk_if_missed: D-146-1 is a data-integrity defect: a memory proposal outliving its workspace is an orphan row that no workspace-scoped query will ever clean up, and it was written by a path that believed the workspace existed. D-146-2 breaks the ordering that crash-safe commit recovery depends on, so a recovery pass can walk the wrong proposal first. Both were invisible for as long as the in-crate test layer could not run, which is precisely why they went unnoticed.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend storage and API behaviour with no operator-visible or model-navigable surface change.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: No command, config key, IPC channel, or navigation path changes. The corrected behaviour restores what the API already documents.

risks: Editing the assertion instead of the behaviour, which converts a real defect into a passing test and is the single most likely failure mode here because all three tests are old and the assertions look arguable.
Fixing D-146-1 by widening the delete transaction in a way that serialises all workspace writes, trading a correctness bug for a throughput cliff.
Fixing D-146-2 by sorting in Rust after the query, which silently breaks the LIMIT assertion the same test makes.
Implementing against the candidate mechanisms this contract lists for D-146-1 without confirming them, since they are explicitly labelled unconfirmed.
Declaring green from a single test run when the failure is a race, so it can pass by luck. D-146-1 in particular is a concurrency test.
minimum_controls: AC-146-4 forbids assertion edits and routes any disagreement to the Operator as a finding.
AC-146-1 requires a measured cause, not the guess written into this contract.
AC-146-5 requires the whole suite, so a fix that breaks a sibling test cannot hide.
The concurrency test must be run repeatedly enough that a pass is not a coincidence, and the number of runs stated.
